questions.q_en: Six persons Ajay, Vijay, Raj, Rishi, Rohit and Ronit are standing in a linear row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Ajay is second to the right of Ronit. Raj is third to the left of Vijay. Rohit is immediate left of Raj. Who is second to the left of Rishi?
questions.solution_en:
Six persons Ajay, Vijay, Raj, Rishi, Rohit and Ronit are standing in a linear row facing north (not necessarily in the same order).

Raj is third to the left of Vijay. Rohit is immediate left of Raj.

Case 1RohitRajVijay
Case 2RohitRajVijay

RohitRajRonitVijayAjay

Therefore, the final arrangement is:

RohitRajRishiRonitVijayAjay

So, Rohit is second to the left of Rishi.

Eight boys are sitting around a square table with their faces towards the centre of the table.

Two boys are sitting at each side.

B is immediate to the right of D.

G is immediate to the right of E. thus, case 2 is invalid.

B is facing H.

Thus, the remaining boy A is facing E.

questions.q_en: In a class of 46 students. Divya's rank from the top was 32nd. If there are eight students ranked between Dev's rank and Divya's rank, then what will be Dev's rank from the top?

Divya's rank is 32nd.

Dev's rank can be 32-8-1= 23rd or 32+8+1 = 41st

So, the rank of Dev cannot be determined.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, two statements are given and two conclusions are given below these statements. Choose the option which shows the conclusions which logically follow from the given statements, disregarding the commonly known facts.

Statements:

All A are B

No B is C

Conclusions:

I: Some B is A

II: No A is C
options_en: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution_en:
Statements:

All A are B

No B is C

Some B is A: All A are B. Thus, Some B must be A. So, conclusion I is true.

No A is C: All A are B. No B is C. Thus, No A is C. So, conclusion II is true.

Hence, both conclusion I and conclusion II follow.
